LESSON: WRITING 1.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Writing 1.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we write clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The skill of working independently as the learner practices forming all the descenders correctly.

Creativity and Imagination: The skill of communication and self-expression as the learner writes words related to the theme in response to picture

prompts.

Values:
Responsibility: Self- drive as the learners ensure their writing is neat and legible through practise.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication as the learner uses the verbs “ to be” in day to day conversations.

Link to other Learning areas:

● Kenyan Sign Language Activities, Mathematical Activities as Sign reading fluency is a key skill to the learner in these learning areas.

● The learner relates the target verb form learnt to Kenyan Sign Language.
